title: Unlimited OCR: Transcribe a Whole Book in One Pass
summary: Unlimited OCR workflows allow users to turn entire printed volumes into editable digital files.
body_markdown:
## Baidu releases Unlimited OCR for full-book transcription


### What is Unlimited OCR?


Baidu Unlimited OCR is a vision-language model designed to ingest entire multi-hundred-page volumes in a single inference pass. By moving away from the fragmented "scan-and-stitch" method, this architecture enables what Baidu calls the " **Era of One-shot Long-horizon Parsing** ."


When a researcher needs to maintain structural context across a 500-page technical manual, they can do so without losing the relationship between a Preface and an Appendix.


While traditional tools struggle with context fragmentation, this model allows for high-volume extraction where the AI understands the "flow" of a book.


Users often pair the raw text output with Activepieces to route the data into long-horizon reasoning models like Claude Fable 5.1. This setup prevents complex agentic work from being tripped up by the formatting errors common in smaller context windows.


### How sliding window attention enables unlimited OCR


The breakthrough that enables this "unlimited" processing is a technical shift in how the model handles visual tokens. Traditional vision transformers suffer from quadratic complexity, where doubling the page count quadruples the computational load, leading to the strict page caps seen in Western cloud services.


Baidu utilizes a specialized linear attention mechanism combined with a sliding window visual encoder. This allows the model to maintain a **constant memory footprint** regardless of document length.


Instead of trying to hold every pixel of a 500-page book in active memory simultaneously, the architecture streams visual features through a recurrent state that carries context forward.


This mechanism functions like a rolling memory buffer that preserves structural relationships without the exponential compute cost. By treating the document as a continuous temporal sequence rather than a static batch of images, the model achieves true linear scaling.


This is why the term "Unlimited" refers to a fundamental architectural efficiency rather than just a large context window.


### Unlimited OCR's October 2026 release details


The October 12, 2026, release of Unlimited OCR marks a departure from the strict page-count throttles imposed by major Western cloud providers. While these platforms bundle OCR as a convenient default, their architectural limits often force developers to chop documents into small, expensive chunks.


Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Gemini 3.1 Pro are the reasoning engines that consume the high-fidelity data these OCR breakthroughs provide.


The disparity in processing capacity is best illustrated by the maximum page limits per asynchronous request:


Provider Pages per request


AWS Textract 3,000


Azure AI Document Intelligence 2,000


Google Document AI 15


*Prices and plan limits checked against[huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/baidu/Unlimited-OCR) and[github.com](https://github.com/baidu/unlimited-ocr) and[docs.claude.com](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/models/overview) and[openai.com](https://openai.com/chatgpt/pricing) and[gemini.google](https://gemini.google/subscriptions) on October 13, 2026.*


Because AWS Textract allows 3,000 pages per job, a user processing a massive legal archive must manage the overhead of splitting and merging thousands of separate PDF files.


Azure AI Document Intelligence supports 2,000 pages, meaning a single large-scale digitization project requires ten times the API orchestration of the Baidu model.


Google Document AI is capped at 15 pages for online requests, which limits its use to short forms and receipts rather than full-book transcription.


You can bypass these platform-specific bottlenecks by deploying Unlimited OCR via[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/baidu/Unlimited-OCR) using NVIDIA GPUs or through[vLLM](https://github.com/baidu/unlimited-ocr) Docker images. This self-hosted approach means the hardware determines the speed of the transcription.
